app/vite.config.ts:5-13 — entire config uses the brand-new Kit 3 pattern: sveltekit() Vite plugin with adapter + compilerOptions
app/src/routes/+layout.svelte:2 — #lib subpath import, the Kit-3-only replacement for $lib
app/vite.config.ts:8-10 — function-form compilerOptions.runes option, merged into Svelte 2026-03-17 (sveltejs/svelte#17951)
app/src/lib/server/api.ts:18-46 — data layer uses plain fetch + Map cache; no experimental remote functions despite being an obvious fit
reach.rationale: Zero experimental/preview/RC APIs, but the app is written centrally in idioms of a stable release that shipped one month ago, plus one ~7-month-old compiler option — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:1-16 — the only non-default framework knob (runes forcing) lives in this single 16-line config file
app/vite.config.ts:8-10 — comment 'Can be removed in svelte 6' explicitly marks the one temporary override for easy removal
app/src/routes/+layout.svelte:2-9 — #lib, $props and @render usage follows one uniform, framework-mandated convention throughout
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; the one custom compiler setting is isolated in a single config file with a removal note, and everything else is the framework's standard, non-optional pattern.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:5-13 — vite.config.ts + plugin-level adapter is the required Kit 3 pattern; svelte.config.js is no longer supported per the migration guide
app/src/routes/+error.svelte:2 — page from $app/state is required since $app/stores was removed in Kit 3.0
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.server.ts:68-69 — error() without throw is the documented Kit 2.16+/3 style
app/vite.config.ts:8-10 — function-form runes replaces the deprecated dynamicCompileOptions and enforces runes mode for all first-party components
app/src/lib/server/api.ts:18-46 — deliberately avoids Kit 3's experimental remote functions, which the official announcement says still need an experimental flag
justification.rationale: Every recently-new API used is the documented current-stable (often mandatory) path rather than novelty, and the app explicitly avoided the one genuinely experimental feature it could have reached for.

findings.issue: The app standardizes on @sveltejs/kit ^3.0.0, a major release only 29 days old; any early-life regressions in Kit 3 would affect every route.
findings.suggestion: Keep caret ranges (already in place) and watch 3.x patch releases; nothing further needed given no experimental flags are set.

findings.issue: The per-filename runes-forcing compiler option is annotated 'Can be removed in svelte 6', referencing an unreleased future major.
findings.suggestion: Leave as-is — this is the officially recommended pattern — but track the Svelte 6 release notes so the override is removed when runes become the only mode.

summary: The app contains no experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs; it is written entirely against the current stable release (SvelteKit 3.0, Svelte 5.57). The only recency is that the stable release itself shipped a month ago and one compiler option dates to March 2026, both used in the officially mandated form. Risk of breaking-change exposure is minimal and confined to standard-version churn, with the one custom compiler setting isolated in a single config file.

experimentalApis.api: sveltekit() Vite plugin config (adapter + compilerOptions in vite.config.ts)
